prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a counter layout extending horizontally in the lower foreground at about 0.4–0.7 metres from the camera wearer, with a cylindrical jar on the bottom left (0.4 m), a keypad/register next to it (0.5 m), a paper bag and snack rack further left (0.8–1.1 m), and a display case on the right (1.0–1.5 m). Directly in front behind the counter, a standing person is positioned roughly 0.9–1.2 metres away, facing toward the camera wearer with the top of their head cropped out in frames 1–4, turning their head to their right (viewer's left) in frame 4 before facing forward again in frame 5 as the camera shifts slightly back. Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's hands and held banknotes rise from the bottom edge into the immediate foreground (brightest white, 0.2–0.4 m away, well within the wearer's arm's reach), increasingly occluding the keypad and the lower torso and hands of the standing person, whose own hands rest on the counter within arm's reach of the register and bills. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the continuous distance gradient across the counter plane, the recessed open room behind the left counter (over 3 m away, dark black), and the step change in depth between the held bills and the person behind them. However, the map looks unreliable in frame 4 where the two separate fan-out stacks of bills and the wearer's right hand merge into a single bloated bright blob, and around thin wire rack structures on the left that blend into adjacent surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map delineates discrete regions in the scene, primarily isolating the standing person centered behind the counter (~1.0 m away, facing the camera wearer with their upper head out of frame) and parts of the foreground counter, jar, keypad, side display case, and the camera wearer's own hands and banknotes at 0.2–0.5 metres. In frames 1 and 2, it segments the lower-left jar (`cup`, ~0.4 m away), the counter surface (`dining table`) and keypad (`keyboard`, ~0.5 m away) in front of the standing person's hands, and the upper-right display case (`tv`, ~1.2 m away, ~0.6 m to the person's left), all within or near arm's reach of both individuals. From frame 3 to frame 5, as the camera wearer raises two stacks of banknotes at 0.2–0.4 metres in front of the lens, these foreground hands and bills occlude the counter and the standing person's lower torso and hands, while the standing person turns their head toward the left in frame 4 and back toward the camera wearer in frame 5. While segmentation makes the exact 2D occlusion boundaries between the foreground held items, the central person, and the background fixtures easier to trace than in motion-blurred RGB frames, its semantic labels and masks are highly unreliable. Specifically, it misclassifies the banknotes as `keyboard` and `laptop` in frames 3–4, merges the wearer's hands and bills into `person` and `laptop` masks, labels the display case and bag as `tv`, `laptop`, and `cat`, and cuts out the center of the standing person's torso mask in frame 5 where the foreground bills overlap.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map tracks the 2D joint topology of the person standing ~1.0 metre in front of the camera wearer and, intermittently, the camera wearer's own right hand in the lower-right foreground (~0.3 m away). In frames 1 and 2, the standing person's symmetric yellow shoulder-to-hip torso trapezoid, bent elbows, and magenta hand skeletons resting ~0.2 metres apart on the counter (~0.6 m from the camera wearer) show them facing directly toward the camera wearer with their arms reaching forward onto the counter and their upper face partially cropped at the top edge. In frame 3, all skeletons drop out completely even though the standing person and the wearer's hands are visible in the RGB frame, and in frame 4 only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's right hand is detected in the lower right while the standing person (who turns their head to the left while occluded below the chest by the raised bills) is missed entirely. In frame 5, the standing person's yellow body and facial keypoints reappear facing and looking toward the camera wearer, with their left hand resting on the counter and their right arm occluded by the wearer's left hand holding bills. The pose map makes the exact wrist and finger articulation of the person's resting hands in frames 1–2 and the wearer's grasping right hand in frame 4 much clearer than in the RGB image, but it is unreliable under foreground occlusion and motion blur, failing to detect the standing person in frames 3–4, missing most of the wearer's hands across the sequence, and distorting the person's lower torso and hand keypoints into yellow leg-like segments in frame 5.
